title: Stream fragment reconciliation: emergency fix for truncated streamed responses and reconnect behavior
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers reported truncated or partially missing outputs when a Server-Sent Events (SSE) connection dropped mid-response. Symptoms included: clients receiving a final 'stream closed' with missing trailing tokens, inability to resume to the same output continuity, and increased support tickets from latency-sensitive apps (fintech and healthcare customers). The issue affected Hosted + Dedicated pools and surfaced in Private deployments behind aggressive NAT/timeouts. Impact: multiple escalations (high-severity) and unchanged SLO breaches for 'complete stream' for rolling windows during the incident window. Repro steps: 1) Start a long generation (>100 tokens) via /v1/stream endpoint. 2) Kill TCP connection at generation token ~N-10. 3) Reconnect immediately with existing session headers (idempotency and resume hints). 4) Observe server replies: either a fresh truncated stream (missing tokens) or an error with no resume. Root cause hypothesis: race between fragment eviction in the KV/fragment cache and stream finalization. The runtime marks last fragment as committed and schedules cache cleanup after a short TTL; under load and some kernel scheduling paths the final fragment wasn't persisted to the fragment ledger before TTL, leaving no authoritative sequence for resumption. Additionally, client reconnection logic expected sequence-contiguous fragments and didn't accept 'overlap' fragments that the server sometimes emitted. Customer escalations: - "Acme Health" reported corrupted discharge summaries (high priority) - "FinApp" reported inconsistent transaction narratives (high priority) Immediate mitigations applied: - Rolled emergency 2s grace-window to fragment eviction to reduce race surface. - Enabled synthetic 'stream-trace' logging for affected host-pools. - Provided customer workarounds: short-lived polling (non-stream) or retry-with-history on SDK. Engineering work: Implemented server-side fragment ledger with sequence numbers and fragment checksums, added a 'final_fragment' marker emitted at stream end, and added a reconciliation flow in the reconnect path: if a reconnect finds a sequence gap, the server will retrieve missing fragments from the ledger and replay them instead of attempting a fresh generation. Also updated client SDK to accept 'resume_hint' semantics (backwards-compatible: if absent, server falls back to legacy behavior). Code changes: see PRs/links below. Canary/rollout plan: canary to 5% first, monitor truncated_response_rate and resume_success_rate for 30 minutes, ramp to 50% for 1 hour, then full. Post-release follow-ups: update public docs about resume semantics, add an e2e test harness that simulates mid-stream disconnects under heavy batching, and add a permanent dashboard tile for 'stream fragment reconciliation success'.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Samira Gupta (PM): Customer reported truncated streaming outputs for long generations (Acme Health). Marking P0. Logged as customer-escalation. Link to incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/INC-2026-031

2026-03-06 - Triage by Asha: Reproduced locally using the stream-fault harness. Observed missing trailing tokens in ~12% of attempts at high concurrency when TTL=500ms. Added temporary extra logging on affected hosts.

2026-03-07 - Liam: Confirmed race between fragment commit and eviction. Built prototype fragment ledger and local proof-of-concept for replay on reconnect. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1782

2026-03-09 - Ops deploy by Priya: Emergency hotfix (grace-window + logging) deployed to hosted-prod and dedicated-hot pools. Noted immediate drop in customer tickets but some Private deployments still seeing issues due to aggressive firewall timeouts.

2026-03-11 - Asha: Edge case found where a reconnect arrives with overlapping fragments and the old client SDK treated overlap as an error. Updated SDK contract and added backward compatibility handling. SDK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/402

2026-03-12 - Liam: Canary rollout started at 5%. Monitoring panels (grafana) updated: truncated_response_rate, resume_success_rate, fragment_ledger_size. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/stream-reconnect

2026-03-14 - Liam: PR 1782 is in review after addressing race by introducing a small synchronous durability step before acknowledging final_fragment. Need one more security review and tests before full rollout.
next_steps: Finish code review + security signoff, expand canary to 50% and validate metrics for 1h, schedule SDK release and notify top impacted customers with detailed remediation steps and timeline, create long-term follow-ups for protocol version bump and fragmentation telemetry.
notes: This ticket focuses on the server-led reconciliation approach to avoid client-side complexity. Long-term we should consider a protocol version bump that exposes fragment checksums so third-party proxies can validate stream continuity.
